title: Cost-aware shard router and deferred prefill autotuner
author: Aisha Reynolds
description:
Motivation: Production workloads show oscillating unit economics when the router aggressively fills GPUs immediately and prefill logic bloats KV caches for low-value short requests. This PR introduces a cost-aware shard router plus a deferred prefill autotuner that (a) biases routing toward lower-cost shards for cost-sensitive requests, (b) defers non-critical prefill work to a background pass when latency SLOs are tight, and (c) exposes an econ_probe for automated A/B simulation and safe rollout.

Summary of changes: Implemented a lightweight cost score in the shard router that combines recent per-shard token cost, observed p95 latency, and current queue depth to compute a routing preference. Added a deferred prefill controller that tags prefill candidates and schedules them using a token-budget-aware background worker; prefill execution is gated by a latency headroom estimator to prevent SLO regressions. Built an econ_probe tool that runs synthetic microbenchmarks against routing knobs and quant profiles to estimate unit cost / latency tradeoffs and produce rollout recommendations.

Checklist and testing: - Unit tests for router scoring logic + edge cases (cold shard, zero-cost shards). - Integration tests that simulate mixed workloads (inference + short completions) and assert p95 latency and avg token-cost improvements. - Bench harness to run econ_probe scenarios and output CSV/JSON results for analysis. - Manual canary on staging with 5% traffic prior to merge.

Commits (high-level): - 1a2b3c4: add cost scoring primitives to shard_router - 2b3c4d5: implement deferred prefill controller + background worker - 3c4d5e6: add latency headroom estimator (rust native) - 4d5e6f7: econ_probe harness + YAML scenarios - 5e6f7g8: python SDK bindings for controller knobs - 6f7g8h9: tests and docs, fix race in worker shutdown

Changed areas (high level): - serving/router: score computation & routing policy hooks - serving/prefill: controller, background worker, and scheduling policy - serving/autotune: econ_probe harness + scenario DSL - ops/benchmarks: new scenarios for mixed short/long workloads - docs/rfc: design and rollout plan - sdk: surface minimal API to adjust cost weight per route

Review conversation (selected): - Marco Chen (reviewer): "Score looks reasonable but we should ensure weight tuning is safe by default. Can we clamp cost_weight to [0,0.5] on main?"
  - Author (Aisha): "Added a config clamp and a runtime feature flag. Default is 0.1 in main; ops can override per-customer. See serving/router/config.go commit."

- Elena Ortiz: "Deferred prefill worker shutdown had a potential race where in-flight prefill tasks could persist after process exit."
  - Author: "Fixed by adding a graceful drain path and force-timeout; added integration test to simulate SIGTERM during prefill. Tests added in tests/integration/prefill_shutdown_test.go."

- Samir Patel: "Econ_probe produced noisy results when quant profiles varied; suggest normalizing by baseline token cost and including variance in the output."
  - Author: "Probe now runs N=20 samples per scenario by default and outputs median + 95th percentile. See ops/benchmarks/econ_sim_runner.yaml and probe output formatter."

CI and stability notes: Initial CI run failed on lint for gofmt and a flake in integration tests (timing related). I fixed gofmt issues and increased the timing cushion on the failing integration test; CI passed on rerun. End-to-end staging canary showed a ~8% reduction in average token cost for the mixed short+long workload used in the benchmark, with p95 latency within target (0ms delta). We observed a small p99 bump in a single scenario; gated rollout and added a conservative default clamp to cost_weight to mitigate production risk.

Rollout plan: - Merge behind a runtime feature flag (econ_shard_router). - Start with 5% traffic canary for seed customers; ops dashboard shows token-cost delta and latency SLOs. - If stable at 48h, ramp to 25% then 100%. Econ_probe scenarios are run nightly for the first week to watch drift and recommend knob changes.

Release notes: "Introduce a cost-aware shard routing policy and a deferred prefill autotuner to reduce unit token cost on mixed workloads. Ship behind feature flag. Improves average token cost while preserving latency SLOs in our bench scenarios."

Why this is different from previous work: Existing batching/quantization PRs tune execution and model profiles. This change targets the request routing and prefill scheduling layer — an orthogonal lever that can reduce unnecessary cache population and steer traffic to more economical shards without modifying model artifacts. The econ_probe bridges routing and quant tuning by simulating their joint impact on unit economics, enabling automated recommendations.

Followups: - Expose route-level knobs in the Console for easier operational tuning. - Add an objective-based autotuner that consumes econ_probe outputs and proposes discrete knob updates. - Investigate using a light RL bandit for per-route cost/latency tradeoffs (experimental).

Related linear/Jira: ENG-2249 (econ routing spike), ENG-2910 (prefill controller), SUP-9123 (customer support case: high-cost short completions).
release_notes: Introduce a cost-aware shard router and deferred prefill autotuner behind a feature flag. Nightly econ_probe jobs provide rollout recommendations and unit-econ insights.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag: econ_shard_router=false by default on main. To enable: update runtime config per cluster. Watch dashboards: route.token_cost_delta, route.p95_latency, prefill.queue_depth. Canary: start at 5% and monitor econ_probe outputs for 48h.
